reason: Three MCP integration defects. (1) _HttpMcpClient built its httpx client with the profile's startup timeout as the read timeout for every request, so a streamable-HTTP tools/call was cut off after startup_timeout_seconds (10 s by default) no matter what tool_timeout_seconds said, and because the failure surfaced as httpx.ReadTimeout rather than asyncio.TimeoutError, McpToolPlugin.execute recorded timed_out=False and the receipt was FAILED with stderr 'ReadTimeout'. _McpClient.request/exchange now take a per-request timeout; the HTTP client sends each request with connect=startup and read=that timeout, call_tool passes tool_timeout_seconds for tools/call, and execute treats httpx.TimeoutException as a timeout. (2) McpProbeService.probe persisted a successful snapshot with the revision read before the network work, inside the catch-all; a concurrent profile edit raised ConflictError there, which was then recorded as a FAILED capability snapshot that discarded the discovered tools. Success persistence now happens after the try/except against the re-read latest revision, so an edit during discovery is merged and a genuine conflict propagates. (3) GatewayClient.request encoded frames with ensure_ascii=True, so a non-ASCII tools/call under the 4 MiB stdin check could grow past MAX_MCP_MESSAGE_BYTES on the Core socket; Core's readline raised ValueError outside the per-message try and closed the only authenticated (single-use bearer) connection, failing every later tool call in the session. Both sides now encode frames as UTF-8 (escaping only for lone surrogates), the shim refuses an oversized frame before writing and returns a JSON-RPC error, and Core skips an oversized frame through its newline and answers with a bounded error instead of dropping the connection. Also, _StdioMcpClient.exchange now waits up to 0.5 s for the stderr reader before composing 'exited during discovery' so the message carries the server's stderr. tests/v3/test_mcp_probe.py gains four tests (HTTP tools/call read timeout equals the tool timeout; an HTTP read timeout is reported timed_out; tools are persisted when the profile changes mid-probe; late stderr is included in the exit message) and the new tests/v3/test_mcp_gateway.py gains three (a 2 MiB CJK argument round-trips although its escaped form exceeds 4 MiB; the shim refuses an oversized request before writing and the connection remains usable; Core answers a raw oversized frame with an error and serves the next request). All seven fail on main.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:core-api (the real-Core journey suite matched through mcp.py and mcp_gateway.py) does not exercise HTTP MCP transports, concurrent profile edits during a probe, or multi-megabyte gateway frames; the Python tests drive the MCP client, probe service, and gateway socket directly. No full suites.
